paper_title: Morphosyntactic probing of multilingual BERT models
caption: Random (light color) and random (darker color) performance comparison with different perturbation setups and the unperturbed trained model variants (orange bars). Left-to-right: Blue: Accuracy of the embedding and first layers' probes; Green: Random models with pre-trained embedding layer: no perturbation, , , , ; Red: Random models where the embedding layer is random as well: no perturbation, , , , ; Orange: Unperturbed trained models.
model_annotation: This bar chart illustrates the accuracy of different model configurations, likely in a natural language processing task. The horizontal axis displays the model configurations, labeled “embedding,” “1st layer,” “random layers,” “random layers +B2”, “random layers +R2”, “random layers +permute”, “random,” “random +B2”, “random +R2”, “random +permute,” and “unperturbed,” presented in that order from left to right. The vertical axis is labeled “Accuracy,” with a linear scale ranging from 70 to 95, and tick marks at 5-unit intervals. The chart consists of 15 individual bars, with the first five bars colored blue, the next five colored green, the following five colored red, and the final bar colored orange. The blue bars representing “embedding” and “1st layer” have heights of approximately 81, 83, 81, and 81, respectively. The green bars, starting from “random layers,” reach heights of approximately 81, 80, 78, 79, and 73, respectively.  The red bars have heights of approximately 72, 70, 71, 70, and 73. The final orange bar, representing "unperturbed", reaches a height of approximately 93. The bars are not visually emphasized with shading, bolding, outlining, or additional annotations.
